subject.title: Compaction should use auth-profile rotation / failover within the same provider

question: Should compaction adopt same-provider auth-profile failover for auto-selected profiles while keeping user-selected profiles locked and applying at most one result to a stable transcript snapshot?
rationale: The behavior matches normal-run auth rotation, but it changes compaction retry/session-state semantics and needs maintainer approval before another implementation attempt.

options.title: Land bounded same-provider failover
options.body: Adopt same-provider-only rotation for auto-selected profiles, keep user pins strict, and require apply-once snapshot protection.

options.title: Narrow the policy first
options.body: Keep this open while maintainers specify a smaller compaction retry contract or additional proof requirements.

options.title: Keep compaction strict
options.body: Decline auth-profile rotation for compaction and document why compaction remains stricter than normal turns.

recommendation.title: Land bounded same-provider failover
recommendation.body: Adopt same-provider-only rotation for auto-selected profiles, keep user pins strict, and require apply-once snapshot protection.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest observed history on auth-profile design, sticky rotation, and current compaction/auth code ownership signals.
